source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS01 is one of Virginia's largest disclosed data centers at 114 MW, but its power source and grid connection are not published.

The facility publishes 114 MW of IT capacity across 685,000 square feet in Sterling, Virginia. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, that is roughly 2,850 racks, though the operator does not specify workload mix or actual tenant configuration. It holds LEED certification, which speaks to energy efficiency standards but not to where the power comes from.

Among the 25 Virginia facilities that disclose megawatt figures, this campus ranks third. Those 25 total 1,603 MW, so Ashburn AS01 accounts for 7.1 percent of the state's published IT load. Virginia has 330 mapped facilities, which means the great majority disclose no capacity at all and remain opaque to public review.

The scale puts the campus in the tier that matters for AI workloads. What cannot be assessed from the published facts is whether its power comes from existing utility supply or new generation, whether it draws on Virginia's grid or a dedicated network, and whether the full 114 MW is allocated or available. Without those three answers, the facility's place in the state's AI scaling constraint stays unknown.
